Methods for zinbreg objects

zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard extractor, summary, and prediction methods for zero-inflated negative binomial fits returned by zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob"),
  at = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (currently ignored).

object, x

An object of class "zinbreg" (or "summary.zinbreg" for the print method of a summary).

signif.stars

Logical; show significance stars?

model

For coef() and vcov(): "full", "count", or "zero".

type

For residuals(): "response" or "pearson". For predict(): "response", "count", "zero", or "prob".

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for the covariates (and any count-offset variables). If omitted, the fitted values are used.

at

For predict(type = "prob"): the counts at which to evaluate the probabilities. Default 0:max(y).

Value

coef(), fitted(), residuals() return numeric vectors; vcov() a matrix; logLik() an object of class "logLik"; nobs() an integer; predict() a vector, or a matrix for type = "prob"; summary() an object of class "summary.zinbreg". The print methods return their argument invisibly.

Details

  • coef(): \(\hat\beta\) and \(\hat\gamma\), either together (model = "full", named count_* and zero_* as in pscl::zeroinfl()) or one part at a time.

  • vcov(): the matching block of the inverse observed information (without \(\log\theta\), whose SE is reported separately).

  • logLik(): the maximized observed-data log-likelihood with attribute df = \(p + q + 1\), so stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work.

  • fitted(): the fitted mean \((1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\).

  • residuals(): response residuals \(y_i - (1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\), or Pearson residuals that divide them by \(\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(Y_i)}\), \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = (1-\pi_i)\mu_i(1 + \pi_i\mu_i + \mu_i/\theta)\).

  • predict(): type = "response" gives \((1-\hat\pi)\hat\mu\), "count" gives \(\hat\mu\), "zero" gives \(\hat\pi\), and "prob" gives the matrix of \(P(Y_i = k)\) for k in at.

  • summary(): coefficient tables for both parts with Wald z tests; the count table also shows \(\log\theta\).

Examples

set.seed(2)
n <- 500
x <- rnorm(n)
z <- rnorm(n)
y <- ifelse(rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + z)) == 1, 0,
            rnbinom(n, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * x), size = 2))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z)
coef(fit)
#> count_(Intercept)           count_x  zero_(Intercept)            zero_z 
#>         0.9657780         0.4698595        -0.9633195         1.0990002 
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -0.9633195   1.0990002 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#> count_(Intercept)           count_x  zero_(Intercept)            zero_z 
#>        0.06541699        0.05525722        0.22574745        0.20567462 
logLik(fit)
#> 'log Lik.' -871.4509 (df=5)
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1752.902
nd <- data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1), z = c(0, 0, 2))
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "response")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 1.1884607 1.9012631 0.9470491 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "zero")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.2762141 0.2762141 0.7746368 
# expected number of zeros
sum(predict(fit, type = "prob", at = 0))
#> [1] 224.6451
